utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, do you wish to cross-examine further?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a proposition for you in the interest of possibly saving time, and that would be that I would not cross-examine further at this time and allow my colleagues to go forward in the normal order. If there is something that is not covered by them, which I doubt, if I could have a few moments at the end, maybe I could do that. I think it will save us some time if we do it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are going to continue with your evidence and we'll move to another counsel who will now ask questions. I simply remind you at the outset that the solemn declaration which you took on Tuesday continues to apply to your evidence today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just have a few questions. I've crossed many of them out because my colleague Mr. Ackerman had already dealt with them. So I'll try to move fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Shaqiri, I am Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law one of the Defence counsel for General Lazarevic. I just have a few questions for you, and I hope that we will complete the cross-examination quickly, if you just give me answers to my actual questions. Yesterday we saw how many statements you gave to the OTP, and I would be interested in the following: In your first statement, you said, in the first statement that you gave to the OTP, namely on the 25th of April, 1999, that in the village of Prilepnica there were 4.500 Muslims and only three Serb families. After that, in your second statement of the 19th and 22nd of June, 2001, also given to the OTP, you said that in your village there are 3.000 Albanians, that there are 40 Roma families, including about 300 people, and now four Serb families you said, not three. During the examination-in-chief, you gave a new figure and you said that there were 30 Roma families in your village and five families -- five Serb families in the village, and while being cross-examined by Mr. Ackerman, you said that there were five or six Serb families. So this is five different pieces of information, and I would like to know ultimately which one is actually correct.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, the word "4.500" was mentioned when I spoke about the people gathered at the border, the number of people deported from Kosova to Macedonia. I didn't mean only the population of Perlepnice. As to the other questions, it's easier for me to answer them if you pose them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Finally, how many Roma families were there in your village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Roma families were over 30. It's an estimate, approximately. And the Serbian family, there is only the Denici family as a family, but each of them have their own houses, five or six. But by this last name, there is only one family. You are asking me about the larger family or the separate -- the narrow families? I don't know what question was asked of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I put a very clear question to you. You were talking about the number of Roma families in your village. I didn't ask you about more or less; I asked you about the total number of Roma families. In the first statement you made no reference to them; in the second one, that there were 40 families; in the examination-in-chief you said there were 30. So I am interested in what is ultimately correct. How many Roma families were there in your village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the accurate figure. It may be from 30 to 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's fine. Thank you. What about Serb --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, sorry, you're going to ask about the Serb families. Yes, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about Serb families? Finally, how many Serb families were there, three, five, or six? Do you know that at all or are you just guessing?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to explain. In terms of a family, an extended family, because a father has three, four children, so it depends on how you look at it. As a family there is only the Denici family, and it consists of four, five houses belonging to that family. That's my answer: Four or five houses belong to the Denici family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many members did that family have?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over 20 members. It's an approximate number, 20 to 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri -- I'm looking at the transcript now, Mr. Shaqiri. A few moments ago you said five or six houses, and now you're saying four or five.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that doesn't seem a significant substantial difference in the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it plainly isn't, but let's hear what the witness's answer is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know the people, but you have to give me some time for me to remember exactly how many they are. Maybe I have forgotten a family. I know that Toza, there are three families.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Shaqiri --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to think -- that's more or less the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If you cannot remember, that's fine. That's fine. If you remember later, that's fine, too. Mr. Shaqiri, do you remember that in your first statement dated the 25th of April, 1999, you said that among the soldiers who came to your village on the 6th of April, that there were quite a few Roma gypsies among them wearing the same uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many, I don't remember to have used the word "many." There may have been some Romas -- there have been some Romas, a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These were the Roma from your village?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know them. Had I known them, I would have mentioned their names, as I did with other people I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, yesterday, during the cross-examination, you said that these Roma families from your village set out together with you in the same convoy; however, in the notes that we got from the OTP, I noticed that you invited them but they did not join the same convoy with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have a reference as to which day? There was a convoy on the 6th and a convoy on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, which day are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The convoy of the 13th, Your Honour. I beg your pardon. I wasn't very accurate on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The convoy of the 14th, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The 14th, in fact, yes.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may explain to you that on the 6th, both of us, we and them, left the village, going to wherever we could. On the 14th -- on the 13th I informed the Romas, too. I did that personally. I conveyed the order given to me to them. During the night, they went somewhere. They were not in the village the next morning, so they didn't leave with us the second day; they did, though, the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, when you returned to the village, did you find any Roma families there or the Serb families there when you returned to your village in June?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the first or the second time?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The second time, that's to say, after you went to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation. The second time we returned from Macedonia in Kosova it was the 25th of June, as far as I remember. And I passed through the village and went to live in Gilac, because there was no place I could live. At the time, I didn't see a single Roma or Serb in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shaqiri. Now I'm going to move on to another topic. I would be interested in the following: Yesterday we talked about what was happening there, and I would like to know whether you know that the barracks in Gnjilane of the regular army with the surrounding buildings was destroyed in the NATO bombing on the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Then you also probably know that the regular army, after this bombing -- or rather, even before the barracks were destroyed, was actually moved out; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My question had to do with Gnjilane, but the transcript doesn't say Gnjilane on page 6, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, it does on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Actually moved out from Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but you've got the reference earlier in line 13. There's no problem with that. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, in your previous statements and also during your testimony here, you said that, in view of the fact that you had served in the military, you knew that the army did not wear red -- or rather, black bandannas and black caps with insignia consisting of four semicircles; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was your answer to that, Mr. Shaqiri?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never subscribed that description to the regular army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shaqiri. You also said to us that on the 6th of April the soldiers who looked that way said to you that they were the regular army, and that later on local people, Palamarevic, Djilas, confirmed to you that they were paramilitaries. And is it also correct that in your notes regarding the 6th you kept calling those soldiers paramilitaries; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe Djilas, and that's why I called them as I did later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Shaqiri, on the 13th of April, only three local persons came to your village in uniform without any insignia, and they said that they were coming on behalf of the regular army. Is that right as well?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And they said to you that they were conveying the decision of the military headquarters in Gnjilane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shaqiri, since we know that the regular army had been moved out of Gnjilane, and when we know all these facts that I have just put to you, actually, except for these words of theirs, you do not have any other reliable proof of the regular army being involved in these events. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only their word because the village was surrounded by the army afterwards and they did not allow us to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shaqiri. Is it also correct that in your second statement given to the OTP on the 25th of February, 2001 - in the Serbian and in the English version it is page 5 - as for the 13th -- rather, the 14th of April, when you were 10 kilometres away from the border and you came across a military check-point, did you not state the following: "From a sharp line we went 6 to 7 kilometres to a water spring and there was a military check-point there. They stopped us and a military officer walked up to me and asked me where we were coming from and why we were fleeing. I said that we were not fleeing, but rather that from the military headquarters in Gnjilane we had been ordered to leave our village." Is this your statement? Are these your words in this statement of February 2001 -- or, I'm sorry, June 2001. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, when you were talking about that particular event at the check-point, during the direct you did not repeat this because it was perfectly clear to you as well that an officer of the regular army would have to have known of the arrival of such a large convoy had the regular army issued such orders; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly - and you actually just confirmed it now - you were issued an order to leave the village, right, not to go beyond the borders of your country; right? That's what you confirmed only a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, yes, but on the 14th of April we were escorted. There was no way -- nowhere else to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These words of yours are from the 14th of April and that's what you said to the officer at the military check-point, that you had received orders to leave the village, nothing more than that; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Shaqiri, we are going to move on to yet another topic and then I will complete my cross-examination very quickly. I would like to know whether you know that in the month of April 1999 the regular army had arrested several local civilians wearing military uniforms and carrying weapons who were introducing themselves as regular army members. I'm giving you the example of the village of Klokot. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Shaqiri. If you don't know, we are going to deal with it during our Defence case. And the last topic: Yesterday -- or no. Rather, first I'm going to ask you something else. In your statement, in the first statement that you gave to the OTP -- rather, the second statement, the 22nd of June, 2001, in response to the question whether there was KLA presence in your area, you said that at that time there was no presence of the KLA in my village or in the other villages in the area of Gnjilane. In Gnjilane, generally speaking, there was no considerable presence of the KLA. I know that you gave a correction stating that it wasn't considerable, but you did not correct this where you said that there were no members of the KLA there at the time in your area. So do you know of any KLA presence in your area at that time?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw KLA presence in Perlepnice and Gjilan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And do you know that in the municipality of Gnjilane, the 171st and the 172nd Brigades of the KLA, involving 1.500 armed men, were operational? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And are you aware of the neighbourhood of Gavran in Gnjilane and the presence of KLA headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You don't know that on the 11th of April, 1999, members of the KLA were arrested - Nazim Maloku and Asim Sofi from Gnjilane? You don't even know that? Asim Sofi admitted that he had taken part in 12 terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about that, sir. I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he's been cross-examined from a document, I don't have that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is based on some information. I'm not going to proceed any further because obviously we are going to get the same answer to all these questions related to each and every particular incident. But I just wanted to know whether this witness knew anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: My last question is, and actually yesterday we discussed it a bit and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, hold on. Mr. Hannis's request is to know which document you're relying on for the propositions you're putting to the witness. If there is a document, then he would like to be alerted to its identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that on the basis of information I received - and I expect that I will get a document as well - but I mean I'm not going to proceed with this examination because obviously the witness doesn't know anything about this, and we'll have ample opportunity to present this during our own case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, indeed, but are you saying you're not in possession of any document on which these questions are based? And by that I mean a document that you're going to be tendering as an exhibit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have any for the time being, but I asked for them. These are reports on security-related incidents, and I expect to receive these documents or this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, carry on then. It's your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very briefly. Yesterday we talked about NATO aircrafts, sorties in this municipality. Mr. Shaqiri, do you know that the NATO air force, from the first days of the war, carried out 113 air-strikes of Gnjilane and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question -- don't answer that question, Mr. Shaqiri. There's no way a civilian in his position would have that information, Mr. Bakrac. These questions, which seem to me to be propaganda based, are not an appropriate form of question for the cross-examination of a witness brought to give this sort of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, very well. I'm not going to ask about the actual figures, but with your permission I'm just going to ask the witness whether he knows of the bombing of the village of Silovo on the 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no knowledge about that, but I saw the military barracks because I happened to pass by. I saw that it was bombarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no questions for Mr. Shaqiri. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- oh, sorry, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe the Ojdanic Defence had asked to go before me with the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't the information I was given, but I'm happy to accept that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It was a late addition, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just as a word of explanation, Your Honour, we thought it might be a little more logical to follow the two army, Colonel Pavkovic, General Lazarevic, and then General Ojdanic. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, my name is Norman Sepenuk, and along with my colleague here Tomislav Visnjic, we represent General Ojdanic. Good afternoon, sir. And I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'm going to focus on only one area and that area is who -- what is your understanding of who ordered you to leave your village on April 13th, 1999? That's the only area I'm going to ask you about. Now, a few days ago, September 5th to be precise, in answer to a question -- in answer to a question from the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis, you said that two Serbian soldiers, Palamarevic and Djilas, told you - and I quote now - "that an order has come from the Supreme Staff in Belgrade. Prilepnica must be evacuated." Do you remember that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And yesterday, in answer -- in answer to a question on cross-examination by Mr. Ackerman, you were referred to your statement of 25 April, 1999 - for the record, Exhibit 4D4 - as to why you left the village on April 13, 1999, and your answer was as follows, and you read from the statement and I quote: "Djilas was the one who had talked. He told me he had orders from the regular Serb army to empty the village." Do you remember that, sir? Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And at that point Judge Bonomy asked you a question about the prior statement you'd made -- actually, he asked you a question about that statement, about the regular Serbian army ordering you to leave the village, and you repeated, you said: "That's correct. Yes, it's correct. This version is correct." And Judge Bonomy said: "Okay." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me. Could you please repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. Judge Bonomy noted that you had testified that the reason you left the village is that you were ordered to do so -- by the way, are you having trouble hearing this? I see you're holding your earphone. Is there a problem, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a page reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, it's page 49, September 6th, lines 8 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Is it okay, sir? Can you hear all right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: If the witness could be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And Judge Bonomy noted in your statement you had said that Djilas had said that the regular Serbian army had ordered you to leave the village, and you said to Judge Bonomy: "That's correct. Yes, it's correct. This version is correct." Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And then a little bit later in your testimony Judge Bonomy noted that answer about orders from the regular Serbian army to empty the village, and Judge Bonomy wanted to know essentially how that related to your prior testimony that it was the Supreme Staff in Belgrade that had ordered you to leave the village. And you said, and I quote, you said: "This is what he said in my presence." I assume that "he" was Djilas. "This is what he said in my presence, that the order has come from Belgrade, from the Supreme Staff, for Prilepnica to be evacuated." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Now, since you testified yesterday we've received other statements that you were authored -- that you authored. We received one statement to a Mr. Morina, an Albanian lawyer, that, as I understand it, you gave in either July or August of 1999, a rather lengthy statement, about 30 pages in Albanian. And then we've also received from the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis, last evening, your questionnaire from the war crimes committee in Kosovo dated October 28th, 1999. And you know what I'm referring to. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And I could go through these statements in some detail, and we could usually -- we can have the usual lengthy, sometimes tedious cross-examination, but I'm going to make an effort to short-circuit this and to streamline it. So I'm asking you, in the interests of time and with the indulgence of the Trial Chamber and Mr. Hannis, to simply take my word for it, that at least three times in this statement that you wrote, the handwritten statement, you said that the orders for you to leave the village came from military headquarters in Gnjilane. You said that at least three times in the statement. I represent that to you. Also, in the interests of time, I represent to you that in your questionnaire that you submitted to the war crimes command -- war crimes committee in Kosovo in October 1999, you said on at least two occasions that you were ordered by military headquarters in Gnjilane to leave the village. So before going into detail - and perhaps not going into detail at all - I'm asking you now, this afternoon, given prior statements that you made, can you tell us what is your best recollection as to why you left your village on April 13th, 1999.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not flee from the village on the 13th but on the 14th, because we had no other way out. And not only once, it was mentioned several times, not only to me but to others as well, that an order has come for Prilepnica to be evacuated. The population wanted to leave, but we were encircled. And the second time, then, under escort, we managed to leave the village. We were escorted to Macedonia, because I had never seen that road before in my life --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now you've left the subject, Mr. Shaqiri. The question is: What is your best recollection as to why you left the village on the 14th? In other words, what's your best recollection of what occurred on the 13th to cause you to leave on the 14th? Now, confine yourself, please, to that very particular question because it's designed to clarify the fact that you've given at least three different versions of what caused that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The order conveyed to us by Palamarevic and Djilas was from the army, and we obeyed that order. The village left under these orders and under their escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So that is your testimony today, that the orders came from the army; correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two, Djilas and Palamarevic, they were militaries. They were wearing military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking you that. I'm simply asking you: What is your best recollection now of what they told you about why you had to leave your village? In other words, who gave the orders?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was conveyed to me and to my village by the two persons that I've mentioned, and what they said was that they had received this order. And I will repeat now what I've said before. They apologised, they said, and I quote: "Forgive us, Hoxha. An order came from Belgrade. Prilepnica must -- must move out." And this is what other fellow citizens were told. And as I said, I wanted someone else to hear this order as well because it is difficult to tell a village with 3.000 inhabitants to leave. This is what I think and this is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So just to clarify, you're testifying now that the order did not come from military headquarters in Gnjilane but rather the order came from Belgrade. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think we are understanding each other or maybe the interpreter is not interpreting it well. I don't know whether it is Gjilan or Belgrade. They were speaking in the name of the army of the name -- in the name of the staff, in the name of Belgrade, and they said: "We are an army and we have to carry out orders."

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did they say that they were speaking in the name of Belgrade, or did they simply say: "We're speaking for the army and you've been ordered out of the village by military headquarters in Gnjilane"?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On whose behalf they spoke, I don't know. They were the ones who conveyed the order. They were speaking for themselves, but they said that the order came from Belgrade and that that order had to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And what particular person or persons in Belgrade gave that order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told by my Serb-speaking colleague here that the witness said in Serbian, in Serbo-Croat, at 18, 2, where it says: "An order came from Belgrade. Prilepnica must --" and it says: "Must move out." I'm told what he said in Serbian is "must be re-settled." And that could be a significant difference, if that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's not one for me to resolve; it can only be resolved with the witness. Just give me a second, please, Mr. Shaqiri. You are quoted here as saying, in reference to the two persons who were conveying the instruction: "Forgive us, Hoxha. An order came from Belgrade. Prilepnica must -- must move out." Now, it's been suggested that what you said in Serbian was: "Prilepnica must be re-settled." Can you clarify the point for us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how it was translated. It has to be evacuated; it has to be clean of people. Now, I don't know what its equivalent in English can be, and from that moment we were under the control of these persons and then we left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That deals with the point. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Now, again, was he any more specific than that, the person -- this is Ljubo, right, or was it Djilas? Who spoke to you, Ljubo or Djilas? We've had different --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djilas, he was the one who did the talking most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Because in your statement - again, I don't want to get into this unless we have a disagreement - in your statement, your handwritten recent statement, you said it was Ljubo who spoke to you. But let's not get hung up on that now, whether it was Ljubo or Djilas. Were they any more specific than that, whether it was Ljubo or Djilas, they said: Belgrade wants you out? Is that what they said? Is that your best recollection today as to what they said?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't say that Belgrade said for you to move out. It's not like this. It was a long conversation, contradictions. Their reasoning was that the order came from the Supreme Staff in Belgrade. This is one of the versions, but they also spoke in other versions. But all versions are linked with Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: What do you mean by "this is one of the versions"? I'm not sure I understand that.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mentioned that the order came from Belgrade; that is one. Secondly, it was mentioned that the order came from the Supreme Staff in Belgrade. Thirdly, it was mentioned that Belgrade ordered for Prilepnica to be evacuated. So this was a long conversation. For me, what is important is the fact that these two persons that I mentioned, with names and last names, conveyed the order and that the following day we moved out under their escort. We didn't do that out of our own free will, but under their orders. We were moved out and sent to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. When you were first asked about this matter in April, April 17th, 1999, you said simply - and I'm looking at now Exhibit 4D9 - you said simply that: "On 13 April, 1999, three identified VJ commanders ordered them to leave the village of Gnjilane." This is the statement that you gave to the OSCE investigator -- it's a statement that you read -- it was read back to you, and you signed it. You testified to that. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this, but it refers to 6th of April. I did not recognise the officers on 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right, but this is -- but right in this report, and again it's Exhibit 4D9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think there is confusion. This actually, according to what Mr. Sepenuk has read to you, refers to the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: The 13th of April, again Exhibit 4D9, originally Prosecution Exhibit 2288, now Defendant Exhibit 4D9, in that statement it talks about circumstances of departure, and it says: "Please describe the circumstances of your departure from Kosovo." And your answer is, which was written down by the person asking you the questions and read back to you and you signed the statement, according to your testimony, your answer was: "On April 13, 1999, 12.00 noon, three identified VJ commanders ordered them to leave the village of Gnjilane." Do you remember giving that statement?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, identified or unidentified? Be clear, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You said: "Three identified VJ commanders," and I assume those VJ commanders, if you'll bear with me, are Ljubo Palamarevic, Djilas Mladenovic and Locki Naskovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And nothing in that statement at all about the Supreme Staff in Belgrade; correct, sir? Are you looking at that statement? I'm representing to you that there's nothing in there about the Supreme Staff in Belgrade. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the need to speak of the Supreme Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then in your statement - and we've had some discussion about this; I'll be very briefly - but in your statement of April 25th, 1999, to Catherine Driguet - and, again, we've been over this - you said it was Djilas who told you that they had orders from the regular Serbian army for you to leave the village. You do remember that? You have to answer audibly. We have to hear you.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will quote: "Djilas, we are the regular army." This is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And nothing in that statement either about Belgrade or the Supreme Staff of Belgrade; take my word on that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I take your word because these are his words, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And then in the statement that you've recently submitted - and I really should ask you a little bit about that because I know very little about it - you apparently submitted a statement to an Albanian lawyer named Morina in July or August of 1999. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in October --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: October of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And it's quite a lengthy statement, 30 pages in Albanian and some 18 or 19 pages in English. And what was the purpose for giving this statement, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Tell us about it. Why did you give this statement to Mr. Morina? Tell us who Mr. Morina is and why you gave him this statement.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Morina collected notes about what had happened in Gjilan municipality, and he asked those who had suffered during the war to give written statements. He collected photographs, other evidence, other names. There are photographs, as I said. Mr. Morina said he was working on behalf of the Tribunal and that every evidence is there with him. So I wrote this statement, and there I described what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you wrote this statement -- by the way, when's the last time you've seen this statement? Have you seen it recently?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No, no, the statement. You submitted the statement now, as I understand it, in about November of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You just wrote it out and handed it to him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And I take it you made every effort to be accurate in submitting that statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all my honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And in that statement you say: "Ljubo Palamarevic -- on April 13th, 1999, Ljubo Palamarevic said, and I quote, 'We apologise, Hoxha, but we have come and we are sent by the military headquarters of Gnjilane to tell you that this village is to be moved completely.'" That's what you said in that statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not recall this version. What I just quoted in Serbian is the correct version. Djilas did not mention Gjilan; he mentioned Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. That's what this statement says, though, that you said "military headquarters of Gjilan". Now, I have a copy of the Albanian statement, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I hand it up to the witness? It's actually in the system, as I understand it, as 4D10, but I'm not sure, because of the shortness of time, whether it can be brought up or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Let's use the hard copy of 4D10.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: There are some matters that are highlighted on that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if that's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Do you see that? And what do the highlighted items say? Do you recognise that, by the way, as the statement that you submitted in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's my handwriting. It's my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And does the underlined portion or the highlighted portion refer to something that Ljubo Palamarevic said?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If necessary, I will read it: "Ljuba looked at me and said: 'We apologise, Hoxha, but we came here -- we were sent by the military headquarters in Gjilan to inform you that this village has to be evacuated completely by tomorrow and that nobody can remain in the village.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's precisely the question I asked you and that is precisely the answer that you gave. So when you gave this statement, you didn't say anything about Belgrade, you didn't say anything about the Supreme Command; you said it was the military headquarters in Gnjilane that had ordered the evacuation. Isn't that true, sir, at long last? Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the conversation, Djilas mentioned not only to me but to the other villagers as well that the order came from Belgrade. I haven't written down every word that Djilas said. It was a long conversation, about one hour long. I have quoted Ljube here, I have quoted Djilas, but I can tell you with full responsibility that Belgrade was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And I can tell you, sir, with full responsibility - unless this is just an atrocious English translation of your Albanian handwritten statement - there is not a single word in the English translation about Belgrade, and there are several other referrals to the military headquarters in Gnjilane ordering the expulsion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'm not going to dwell on it anymore, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think it's important just to ask one thing for clarification, and I'm looking for the reference in the testimony. I'm not finding it in the -- but I have a note here that the witness said: "I don't recollect saying that Djilas mentioned Gnjilane, he said Belgrade." Now, have I wrongly noted that down as part of his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No, I think he said that, but -- because Djilas was the one who did say, and we have a statement, that the regular Serbian army is the person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can anyone help me find it on the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, it's on page 25, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm much further back. Thank you. Well, is that -- no, I don't think that -- that doesn't seem to be the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's at page 24, line 4: "Djilas did not mention Gjilan; he mentioned Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Shaqiri, you have told us that Djilas did not mention Gnjilane, and yet here we have the very first statement that you gave saying that specifically. And you say: "I have quoted Ljube here, I have quoted Djilas, but I can tell you with full responsibility that Belgrade was mentioned." But what you've actually concentrated on in the statement was Gnjilane and you've told us today that that wasn't mentioned. Now, can you explain that apparent contradiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the conversation of the two officers didn't take place only with me but also with others who raised objections to our moving out. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me make it more simple for you. Obviously my question was too complicated. Did one of these officers mention Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they mentioned Gjilan and Belgrade, both, and several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why did you earlier in your evidence say that Gjilan was not mentioned? Or at least you said: "I don't recollect saying that Djilas mentioned Gjilan."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ljuba said that the order comes from Gjilan, whereas Djilas said that the order comes from Belgrade. These are the two versions they both mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I want to go to the next statement, which is the one you submitted on October 28th, 1999. It's actually part of a questionnaire of war crimes committed in Kosovo. It's a number of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I have an English translation of it, and I'll ask Mr. Hannis, is there anything in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think all we have is that English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And that, by the way, Your Honours, is 4D11.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And in this statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may request that some foundational questions be asked about this statement, because all I do have is the English and I don't think it's signed and I don't know the circumstances in which it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'll be happy to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman - and I may be mispronouncing the name now - Vjollca Musliu, M-u-s-l-i-u? Does that name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the moment it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: He supposedly was a member of the central war crimes commission in charge of gathering evidence, and according to this document that I have that I only received last night at about 6.00 p.m. He interviewed you in Prilepnica on October 28th, 1999. He said your occupation was teacher, imam of the village. And he asked you a number of questions relating to alleged war crimes. Does this ring any kind of a bell? Does this register with you at all?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You don't remember being interviewed by this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And do you know any other Abdylhaqim Shaqiri - I know I've pronounced that terribly, and I apologise for that - a male person from "the birth place of Perlepnice, north of Kosovo; Albanian ethnicity; citizenship: Kosovar; occupation: imam." Do you know any person by that name, other than you?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no other imam in Perlepnice and in the other villages other than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, the document that I have goes into all of the matters that have already been testified to, names like Ljubo Palamarevic, Djilas Mladenovic, Naskovic, et cetera. On the other hand, if you deny that you're the person who was interviewed --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I would have hesitation, Your Honours, about going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Do you have true doubt that you were the person interviewed by the central war crimes commission?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned Abdylhaqim Shaqiri and Vjollca Musliu, I don't know them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Because this says the same thing as all the other statements have been saying, that "on April 13th, 1999, we were ordered by the military headquarters in Gjilan to move from the village"; totally consistent with your other statements. So again, finally your comment would be you don't want to take responsibility for this statement, or you have no recollection of it, or it might be inaccurate? I'll leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I have no recollection, I can take no responsibility for that. If I remember, I will certainly take responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it possible that you said to an interviewer around October 1999 that on the 13th of April you were ordered by the military headquarters in Gnjilane to move from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, each time we talked, on different occasions we repeated what happened. Maybe that person was present in a certain place where we talked about that and maybe he has taken notes. I have no idea about that because this doesn't ring any bell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, but my question is a more general one. Is that a statement that you could have made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no answer. I don't remember anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me ask you it in a different way. In the conversation you had with those who were giving the order to you, was any reference made to military headquarters in Gnjilane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was mentioned. With Djilas, it was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'll move on to a statement I don't think there's any doubt about, at least I don't think so, and that's your statement of June 19th, 2001, to Ann Murtagh, Exhibit 4D6, in which on page 4 thereof you said that the army reserve officers -- you said you knew two of them, and I'm sure we're talking about Ljubo and Djilas and one other person now. The army officers said: "They were only conveying the orders of the military headquarters in Gnjilane" when they told us to leave the village. Do you remember that statement? Is your answer yes?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Nothing in that statement about the Supreme Staff in Belgrade; correct, sir? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing because I didn't deem it appropriate to mention it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the statement -- your interview of 5 February 2001, which is Exhibit 4D5, and in which you wanted to correct a number of mistakes that were made in your prior statements, again, I'll simply represent to you that there's no mention in that statement of orders coming from Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And then finally in your statement to the Prosecutors on 28th August 2006, Exhibit 4D8, there is some 27 corrections and additions to the statement. In part 11 of the statement you spoke about Ljuba Palamarevic, again one of the three Serbian officers, and you said that the 2001 statement describes him as a judge, "and Mr. Shaqiri states that the person was a lawyer but became a judge prior to April 1999." But nothing again about orders from Belgrade; correct? The answer is yes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So the fact is that there is not a single word in any of -- all of your prior statements, not a single word by Djilas, Ljubo, or anybody else that any order came from Belgrade - is that a fair statement - in any of your prior statements?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I mentioned it somewhere, but I am repeating it. This is what Djilas said; that was a reason he gave to us for ordering us to move out, that is, the order had come -- and I'm saying this in full moral responsibility, namely that this is what Djilas told us: "We are a regular army. We received orders from Belgrade for Perlepnice to be evacuated." Whether he said it just to cover up what he was doing or for anything else, this is I don't know. You can ask him; he is alive. He can express what he thinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you prepared notes to your testimony here today, did you not, sir? You prepared notes?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did you have notes -- maybe I missed -- maybe I misunderstood. At the beginning of your --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The question was today. He may have misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Before you testified - let me clarify that - before you testified, is it true that you had prepared notes to assist you in testifying?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have them with me, but I'm telling you, I wrote down the names of the persons I have mentioned in case I wouldn't remember them for some reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. But I'm not interested in that. I simply want to ask you whether again you did make notes in preparation for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You did not make notes -- you didn't have notes with you when you first started to testify? Remember when Mr. Hannis first started to ask you questions --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. I didn't understand you right, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the statements with me. I only got with me some statistics from the municipality, thinking they would be of help to me. And I left them at the hotel. Now I saw that I -- that they were of no use here, things about -- statistics about what happened in the Gjilan municipality, which I have with me in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm just asking you a general question, that you did prepare some notes in preparation for your testimony here; correct? Is the answer yes?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And we know that -- Mr. Hannis said, "Put them aside." The Prosecutor told you to put them aside and use them only if you needed them to refresh your recollection, and you did put them aside and I don't think you ever referred to them again. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you were preparing to testify in this trial, as any witness might; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time for me to appear in a court as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you know about this trial? I'm asking you: What did you read in the media -- I mean in the newspapers? What did you hear on television? What did you possibly hear on the internet, the media, the news services? What did you know about this case before you got here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My life's too short for that question, Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has a definite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but it must be a more precise version --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did you know of --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'll ask -- and I'll be more precise. My life's even shorter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, looking around, that's very encouraging.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I say that -- I say that sadly and very respectfully, needless to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did you know who the defendants were in this case, the accused? Did you know who the accused were before you got here? Before you got here, and when you got here, do you know who's on trial here?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Often we read, whenever we can, what is going on in the Hague Tribunal. Our media is rather limited, I mean the Albanian-language media, and it reports very little about what is going on in The Hague for the moment. When the trial of Mr. Milosevic was being on, the media coverage was greater, but not so much now. Very rarely you can see something being written about the trial here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Do you know that there's six men sitting in the back of this court-room. They are the so-called accused in this case, the defendants in this case. Do you know about any of them? Do you know about one -- all of them, all six? Do you know who they are? Are they sergeants? Colonels? Majors? Privates? Who are they?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Who do you know?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic, I've never talked to them, of course, but I've seen their faces on television or on the newspapers. I know the general by sight, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Which general?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the television. Ojdanic, General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The others I can't see from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Mr. Milutinovic, have you ever heard his name?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard the name, but I -- you prevent me from seeing him or -- I don't know. Yes, now I see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you know, then -- and Mr. -- General Pavkovic, General Lazarevic, these are names that are known to you; correct? General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about them. I don't know, I think about General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you know, then, that the six accused on trial here are rather very high-up political, military, and police figures. Is that correct, sir, you know that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they used to be high-up figures, but I don't know them to be now in the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But is it fair to say they're considered by you to be part of the Supreme Staff of Kosovo, and that your testimony -- you're testifying today with respect to those alleged Supreme Staff members? Is that in your mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's irrelevant to you - is that right - the fact that they are high-up political, military, and police figures? That has nothing to do with your testimony that allegedly the order to leave your village came from the Supreme Staff in Belgrade? That has nothing to do with your testimony; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, sir, you are putting it wrong. I didn't say that the order came from Belgrade, but that it was Djilas who said to us that the order came from Belgrade. I and my people suffered it on our backs. I don't want any people to be tried. There is no bad people in the world. Only those who have committed crimes should be held responsible for what they have done. Who is innocent, let him enjoy his freedom; who is guilty, let him be held responsible. I am not here to try a general or anyone else; I am here to recount to you what happened to us. The mosque I serve is burned. The library which was there for over 150 years was burned. And all -- the damage is worth over 20 million Deutschmarks. This damage was inflicted there by someone. So if these people are to blame, let them be held responsible because someone is responsible and it is up to this Tribunal to find the culprits. That's my answer. I am not here to blame anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I certainly agree with your comment that it's up to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Shaqiri. My name is Dan Ivetic, and together with my colleagues Branko Lukic and Ozren Ogrizovic, I represent Serb police general Sreten Lukic. It's my job here today to ask you some questions to clear up some matters pertaining to your testimony that we've heard here the past couple of days, and I'll try to make my questions as concise as possible so we can go through this smoothly. I would ask you to give me the most truthful answer possible, and if you don't know the answer, just say so. Now, first of all, I want to clear up some things you testified about the other day. On Tuesday you mentioned several times the "local police." For example, you talked about the local police from Kamenica, how they communicated the information they received from the SUP that you could return to your village. Now, when you use the term "local police," are you referring to employees of the Ministry of the Internal Affairs, that is to say the MUP, of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For me the police of Kamenice. I don't know how to answer you. The regular police of Kamenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "the regular police of Kamenice," are you talking about people from the MUP? Are you familiar with the abbreviation MUP?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say the "local" or the "regular police," are we talking about the MUP, people from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, in fact, the regular -- let's focus on the police from Kamenice for a second. These police from the MUP from Kamenice, they had authority over the entire Republic of Serbia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now, with respect to the police from Kamenice, when you described that the police from Kamenice told you to go back to your village, did you understand this as the police trying to help you and your people? Did you view it as a good thing?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a very good thing indeed, I may say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now, with respect to your travels that day, is it accurate to state that you went through several traffic check-points and that through these -- that some of these check-points were manned by the Serbian MUP police? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The check-point is something else. There were traffic police in Kmetofc and soldiers some 50 metres away, regular soldiers. I mentioned that earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What I want to ask you about is: Is it a fact that at no point in time did any member of the Serbian MUP mistreat either you or any of the villagers that were under your care in the convoy? And now we're focussing on the first convoy of April the 6th, 1999.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody mistreated us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were heading towards the municipality in Serbia known as Bujanovac. Am I correct in stating that this municipality has a majority ethnic Albanian civilian population?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you clarified yesterday that there was no actual -- that there was -- that there was no actual border crossing between Kosovo and the rest of Serbia. Am I correct to say that there is a police check-point at Konculj that is regarded as the informal administrative line between the Bujanovac municipality and the municipalities in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the word --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Konculj is far. I don't know. We didn't go up to Konculj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the word you used was informal --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's been corrected, Your Honour. I noticed that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question for you. So your convoy did not reach Konculj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We only passed by -- I don't know whether it was 100 or 200 metres away from the administrative boundary. I am afraid to mention figures because figures are creating problems for me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try to avoid that where it's not necessary, and I think for now we can move on. Now, on Tuesday you described that when you returned to your village on the 7th of April, that thereafter on the 9th and 10th of April, "we stood guard with the police from the town." And I presume by "we" you meant persons from the village. And I wanted to, first of all, ask you: Am I correct that by "police from the town" you mean members of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the MUP of Gjilan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And could you explain for us, sir, when you and your people returned on either the 6th or the 7th of April - I know people came at different times - did anyone have any problems with the police, that is to say with the MUP, who were in fact there in the area?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nowhere have I mentioned that we had problems with the police. I have only stated that they always helped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, just to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it's time for the break. But that answer is not good enough for you, Mr. Ivetic, we've still got more cross, have we?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour, but I hope to be able to complete my cross within, I'd say, maybe half an hour of the next -- I'll try to be brief. I'll endeavour to try and curtail the questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for future transcript readers who might be trying to search for things, I understand the municipality Gjilan is spelled with an "N" in both Serbian and Albanian, not "Gj" but "Gnj" in both cases. It's showing up in the transcript as "Gj", which can throw somebody off trying to do a search for Gnjilane. I don't know if that is helpful to anybody or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what you're suggesting is that there's an inaccuracy in the indictment? If we look at 72(i), which is one of the paragraphs we're directed to, it's spelled in the Albanian without an "N".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: In Albanian it's correct, "Gj".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the interpreter is telling me on the earphones that in Albanian it should be spelled "Gj".

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's what I just heard, Your Honour. Yesterday you criticised my colleagues here for not helping me. Today they've been helping me, and I'm not sure if it's of any use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no -- anyway, it looks as though anyone searching will have to undertake both to be sure, and we shall resume at ten past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shaqiri, now, when we left off, we had talked about the conduct of the police with respect to the civilian population. I want to focus for a moment on the time period during 1998, and I would ask you: During 1998, did you have the same -- strike that. During 1998, what was the general atmosphere like in Gnjilane municipality vis-a-vis the civilian population and the Serbian MUP or the Serbian police? How was their interaction?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak of my own village, not about the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's fair. You could speak about your village. And would it also be fair to say that you could speak about the other two villages that you were also the imam of?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot with great responsibility. Something could have happened in those two villages. But, as I said, for my own village I can speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be fair to say that with respect to your own village there were not any such problems with the Serbian police during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my village never did have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And during 1998, did you know of any or witness any conflicts or fighting between the Serbian police and any armed groups in the area, such as the KLA/UCK?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now I'd like to move on back to 1999. And the other day you mentioned the customs police in your testimony. Now, I want to ask you: In 1999, the Republic of Serbia, including Kosovo-Metohija, was part of a federal state known as Yugoslavia. Is that correct -- actually, I strike that. I just want to say: Would it be accurate to state that in 1999 the customs officials operating at the international borders of Yugoslavia were federal officials, that is to say Yugoslav personnel, and not personnel of the Republic of Serbia. Do you have knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew them as customs officials. As for whether they were Yugoslav personnel or Serbia's personnel, for me they were officials of Serbia, or Kosova, better to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You described the gentleman that was the customs chief having a solid uniform. Did that uniform have any badges or insignia; and if so, could you describe them?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've forgotten the insignia, sir. He was about 60 years old, and somebody said that he was from Kllokot, but he may not be from Kllokot as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I could just focus -- and I think I have just one more question with respect to the uniform after you verify this for me. Was it your testimony -- is it your testimony that his uniform was a solid colour, that is to say solid as opposed to camouflaged?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Solid colour, police, tidy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And the last question I want to ask you with respect to uniforms, sir, is: Isn't it a fact that the Serbian police from the MUP had blue camouflage uniforms and badges?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that place. As for the whole territory of Kosovo, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "not in that place," are you saying that the personnel at the border did not have blue camouflage uniforms? Is that --

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you testified about some vehicles that were left at the border and I want to ask you: Had you had occasion to travel outside of Yugoslavia prior to that occasion at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if I had an occasion to travel, personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, do you have knowledge of the fact that in order to travel with a vehicle outside of Yugoslavia, there are certain documents or registrations, including insurance certificates, that need to be obtained and presented to allow a vehicle to pass the international border?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is it also a fact that since your convoy of people had not been given much time to prepare to leave, that this necessary documentation was lacking?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. With all my respect, I can tell you that there were vehicles who had the whole documentation necessary there. We calculated later on that 518 vehicles, tractors, motor-cultivators, trucks, and trailers attached to tractors and motor-cultivators remained there. I had my vehicle with all documentation necessary, but I was ordered to leave the keys and the documents in the car and to continue on foot to cross the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That clears things up. Now, I'd like to ask you with respect to -- do you know if any other groups actually passed the border in their vehicles? Do you have knowledge of that or is your knowledge limited?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have a knowledge that a group left by cars. All the vehicles remained there at Gllobocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the past few days you've referenced the "military police," and I just want to first clear up some confusion in my own mind in that regard based on the testimony. I'm not sure what the end result is, but I want to make it clear with you. The military police that you talked about, are they a part of the Serbian MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, as you understand it, or not?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you -- you said that your brother was a reservist. Was he a reservist in the Ministry of Internal Affairs or was he a reservist in the army?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. Until 1985/1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether he was a reservist in the police, the military -- excuse me, the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the police, or in the army? At that time I guess it would have been still the JNA, the Jugoslovenska Narodna Armija?

utterances.speaker: ABDYLHAQIM SHAQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a driver in the GNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to move to another topic. Yesterday -- I think it was either yesterday or Tuesday you talked about three individuals that went to try and contact the police on the 13th of April, 1999, the day before you left your village the second time. And I want to know whether you know -- you said you didn't know the name of the policeman that they spoke with, that you forgot it, but do you know whether the policeman that was spoken to, whether that was an ordinary policeman, or was he someone with some sort of superior rank, that is to say in the Serbo-Croat, an "staresina" of the MUP?
