utterances.text: No, Your Honour. He's talking about the general train schedule, how many trains went on an average. You can see from the log-book that the number of trains increased. You can read from his testimony about how additional cars were put on and additional passengers were going. You've heard the testimony from people from Pristina who got on the trains and travelled to Urosevac and Ferizaj during those dates. So it corroborates their information as well about how they were packed on the trains and how many were going, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Bucaliu, one thing that you told us about the way in which this log-book is kept was that where there was an arrow through the time of arrival of a train, that indicated that the train did not stop at the station. But I notice in these cases that the time of departure is completed in each case. Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can ask him a question about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Bucaliu, did you hear what the Judge just said? You've indicated on those entries where there is a diagonal arrow through the arrival time that the train did not stop in Ferizaj, but there is a time under the departure column. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BAJRAM BUCALIU
utterances.text: This means -- that is, the arrow shows that the train passed through the station at the time indicated here, at column 5 and 6. The arrow indicates that the train passed but did not stop, because if it stopped, it should be indicated at column 3 and 4. So the arrow only says that the train has passed the station without stopping.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the time refers to the time it passed through?

utterances.speaker: BAJRAM BUCALIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right, the time it passed. According to the schedule, all the passenger trains, irrespective of whether they were regularly scheduled or otherwise, they had to stop at Ferizaj station. But many trains didn't stop, even though they were passenger trains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So that was unusual. They were required to stop whether a passenger had requested to get off or not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BAJRAM BUCALIU
utterances.text: Yes, that was unusual. As I said, every passenger train stopped normally at Ferizaj station because this is considered a major station. Even the international trains stopped there when they ran, or the ones that travelled off to Junik. So every passenger train has to stop because somebody will get on or off the train.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bucaliu. I think we've got the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would like to tender Exhibit 1331. I have no more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that the only exhibit referred to in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour. I'll have to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know there was one other exhibit referred to in his testimony. He had a hand-made drawing of his village, the houses in the village. I didn't think it was necessary for Your Honours to understand his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it have a P number in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, it does not. We can certainly provide it to you, but it was my assessment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I mean -- the problem is it may be of interest to the Defence, for all you know, I suspect. So in these cases it's probably best that we have the exhibits. It doesn't matter on this particular instance at the moment. We shall see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I shall consult with them if they need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give me an order, Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. General Lazarevic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Milutinovic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, and General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bucaliu, we have to finish for this evening and adjourn the case until tomorrow, but it will continue and your evidence will continue at 9.00 tomorrow morning. So you have to be back here in time to start giving evidence again at 9.00 tomorrow. Meanwhile, it's very important, as you will know from the previous case, that you do not discuss your evidence with anyone. And by that I mean the evidence you've already given us and any evidence that you are likely to give us tomorrow. You can talk about anything else with anyone you meet, but you must not discuss the evidence with anyone. All right? So we will see you again tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 8th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
